name: Battle of Shanghai
note: This plan shows the whole operation, not a single field: each block is an army, a corps or a fleet, and the towns, creeks and the river are the ground it was fought over. The accounts give only rough directions and distances, so the positions are schematic. Many Chinese and Japanese divisions are folded into the formations the accounts name most often; the accounts do not say which Japanese divisions stood where at each date.

phases.title: The Chinese assault on the Japanese garrison in the city
phases.text: Chinese divisions attacked the Japanese naval landing force in Zhabei and towards the Huangpu docks, and the 36th Division joined them. The Japanese Third Fleet shelled the attackers from the river, and the Chinese were halted short of the water.
phases.quote: By August 21, 1937, Chinese tanks had managed to punch through to Broadway, the last street before the Huangpu.

phases.title: Japanese troops land on the coast
phases.text: The Japanese 3rd and 11th Divisions landed on the north-east coast under naval bombardment, and the Chinese brought troops from the city to meet them. The front line was lengthened from the city to the coast.
phases.quote: the Japanese 3rd and 11th Divisions made an amphibious assault under the cover of naval bombardment and proceeded to land

phases.title: The fight for Luodian
phases.text: The Chinese concentrated around Luodian and the Japanese came inland against them with naval gunfire, tanks and aircraft. The Chinese were bled almost dry and gave up the town by the end of September.
phases.quote: To defend Luodian, the Chinese concentrated some 300,000 soldiers there, while the Japanese amassed more than 100,000 troops

phases.title: The Japanese reach the Wusong Creek
phases.text: The Chinese fell back to the south bank of the Wusong Creek, and the Japanese attacked across it. The line was breached after two days at one bridge, but the Japanese met further defences behind it.
phases.quote: On October 5, 1937, the Japanese forces smashed into the Chinese defenses across the Wusong Creek

phases.title: The Guangxi counteroffensive
phases.text: The Guangxi Army joined the line and counterattacked to retake the banks of the creek. It was poorly coordinated and bogged down, and the Japanese answered with artillery, tanks and poison gas.
phases.quote: These Guangxi units, four divisions in total, then staged a final counteroffensive on October 21

phases.title: Dachang falls and the Chinese leave the city
phases.text: The Japanese pushed on to Dachang and took it. The Chinese then withdrew from downtown Shanghai, which they had held for almost three months, to a line behind the Suzhou Creek.
phases.quote: The fighting continued until October 26, when Dachang finally fell.

phases.title: The Japanese cross the creek and land at Jinshanwei
phases.text: The Japanese crossed the Suzhou Creek, and the Chinese were in danger of encirclement. On 5 November the Japanese 10th Army landed at Jinshanwei on Hangzhou Bay, behind the Chinese line.
phases.quote: to land easily in Jinshanwei on November 5, 1937
